blocking_findings.summary: ASKFLOOR-1-T2b-AC3: NEW `shared/permission-prospective-write.ts` (shared layer, filesystem-backed like `shared/permission-hard-boundaries.ts`) exports `evaluateProspectiveWriteBoundary({ workspaceRoot, candidatePath }) → Promise<{ inside: boolean; reason?: string }>`: lexical containment after normalisation; the nearest EXISTING ancestor realpath-contained in the realpath of the root; no symlink component and no symlink target (`lstat`); a non-existent target allowed; and the three protection checks by import — `isProtectedCapabilityPathLike` (`shared/tool-execution-protected-paths.ts:40`), `hasHiddenPathSegment` (`shared/auto-permission-read-only-catalog.ts:143`), `isSecretLikeValue` (`shared/permission-hard-boundaries.ts:83`) — applied to the candidate relative to the root. FAIL-CLOSED, TOTAL: boundary uncertainty never throws through permission evaluation — a missing, non-absolute or unresolvable root (IPC supplies a syntactically resolved path without proving it exists, `platform/workspace-folder.ts:21-25`), and any `realpath`/`lstat`/filesystem error all return `{ inside: false, reason }` (the pattern of `permission-hard-boundaries.ts:33-52`). A NON-ABSOLUTE candidate is provider-relative and is resolved against the verified workspace root BEFORE evaluation (`path.resolve(root, candidate)`; the deepagents facade accepts only relative paths and forwards that `{ path, … }` input to permission IPC, `shared/gantry-tool-facades.ts:455-475`, `gantry-facade-tools.ts:121-130`) — so `notes/a.md` inside is `low` and `../x` is `high`; only a non-absolute ROOT fails closed. NEW `application/permissions/native-file-write-risk.ts` exports `judgeNativeFileWrite({ toolName, toolInput, workspaceRoot }) → Promise<{ verdict: GantryToolRiskVerdict; reason: string }>` (the reason is the boundary's `reason` or a fixed string per rule, copied into the classifier result): accepts exactly `FileWrite`/`FileEdit`; destinations are EVERY non-blank string among `file_path` (Anthropic runner, `tool-permission-gate.ts:621-674`) and `path` (deepagents facade, `gantry-facade-tools.ts:110-132,160-189`) — when both are present both are evaluated and the verdict fails closed (`high` if any destination is not inside); `low` only when every supplied destination is inside and unprotected; `high` when any is outside, protected, hidden, secret, symlink-involved, or `workspaceRoot` is undefined; `ambiguous` when no string destination is supplied. `gantry-facade-file-safety.ts:39-67` stays the execution-time authority and is not imported (async, config-bound, creates directories); T2a's `evaluateReadHardBoundaries` is not reused (it checks EXISTING read targets). The eligibility gate (`application/permissions/permission-classifier.ts:11-28`) gains an optional `lane` parameter and accepts `FileWrite`/`FileEdit` ONLY when `lane === interactive_auto`, evaluated before today's exits; with the lane absent or any other value those ids stay ineligible, so `consultPermissionClassifierBeforePrompt` returns today's `undefined` and emits nothing (the classifier passes its input's optional `lane` to the gate). The native-risk helper routes those two ids to `judgeNativeFileWrite` and gantry names to the table. Tests: inside → allow with no LLM call (each key alone, absolute and provider-relative such as `notes/a.md`; `../x` → ask); conflicting dual keys (inside `file_path`, outside `path`) → ask; outside, protected (`settings.yaml`), hidden segment, secret name, symlinked parent, symlinked target, a symlink-plus-dot-segment path such as `link/../victim` where `link` points outside (review round 1: the RAW candidate is inspected for `..` segments before any `path.resolve` collapse and fails closed), unresolvable root, non-absolute root → ask; missing target inside → allow; no string destination → ambiguous → LLM consult; `FileRead` stays ineligible; `FileWrite` under `auto_strict` or with the lane absent → ineligible, `undefined`, no event.
